### Equivalence and cost

```{python}
#| label: warm-start-gates
if RUN_WARM_START_VERIFICATION:
    force_cold, spread_cold = mean_shell_force(cold_shifted_network, shifted_state)
    force_warm, spread_warm = mean_shell_force(warm_network, shifted_state)

    equivalence_check = mfp.warm_start_equivalence_gate(force_cold, force_warm, force_tol)
    cost_ratio = mfp.warm_start_cost_ratio(cold_shifted_history, warm_history)
    cost_check = mfp.evaluate_check(
        "Warm-start cost ratio", "Optimizer evaluations of the warm run over the cold run",
        cost_ratio, 1.0, "<",
    )

    warm_probe_losses = mfp.diagnose_loss_scale(
        warm_network, domain, fluid_config, held_out_config,
        z_shifted, particle_radius, PEAK_VELOCITY_NONDIM, **SHELL_ARGS,
    )
    warm_probe_gap_check = mfp.generalization_gate(
        warm_history.final()["total"], warm_probe_losses["total"], PROBE_GAP_TOLERANCE)

    for check in (equivalence_check, cost_check, warm_probe_gap_check):
        verification_checks = verification_checks + (check,)
        verification_categories[check.name] = CONVERGENCE
    mfp.render_verification_table((equivalence_check, cost_check, warm_probe_gap_check))
```

```{python}
#| label: warm-gates-prose
#| output: asis
# CHANGED: emitted from Python; the interpolations are valid only when the
# section ran.
if RUN_WARM_START_VERIFICATION:
    print(f"At the shifted position the cold run gives a force of {force_cold:.4f} and the "
          f"warm run {force_warm:.4f}, a relative difference of "
          f"{equivalence_check.metric_value:.3%} against a tolerance of {force_tol:.2%}. "
          f"The equivalence gate therefore "
          f"{'clears' if equivalence_check.passed else 'misses'}. The warm run needed "
          f"{cost_ratio:.2f} times the optimizer evaluations of the cold run, and its held-out "
          f"probe loss stays {warm_probe_gap_check.metric_value:.2f} times its training loss. "
          f"The shell spreads of the two runs are {spread_cold:.1%} (cold) and {spread_warm:.1%} "
          f"(warm); a force difference below these values cannot separate a warm-start effect "
          f"from the intrinsic scatter of the traction.")
else:
    print("No warm-start equivalence or cost gate is reported: the section was skipped.")
```

The two resistance problems are never warm-started from each other. Their errors
enter $U_\text{free} = -F_0/F_1$ with opposite signs and partly cancel, and that
argument holds only if the errors are independent. In
`resistance_position_sweep`, each problem is initialized from its own
counterpart at the previous position.

## Faxén-limit consistency

```{python}
#| label: check-faxen-consistency
# CHANGED: the tolerance is no longer the gap between two nearly identical series (0.03 %).
# It is the reference uncertainty, floored by the Oseen estimate. Faxén's law is a free-space
# result, so it is reported for information and is not the gated reference at lambda = 0.25.
faxen_probe = torch.tensor([[1.0e-3 * R, particle_axial_position]], device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
faxen_velocity = float(mfp.faxen_corrected_velocity(baseline_network, faxen_probe, particle_radius)[0, 1])
passive_error = abs(u_passive - refs["force_free_velocity"]) / abs(refs["force_free_velocity"])
faxen_check = mfp.evaluate_check(
    "Passive velocity against the wall-corrected reference",
    "Force-balanced velocity of a passive sphere vs. the series reference U_free = u_c K_P / K_H",
    passive_error, reference_tol, "<=",
)
verification_checks = verification_checks + (faxen_check,)
verification_categories[faxen_check.name] = VALIDATION
mfp.render_verification_table((faxen_check,))
```

For a parabolic ambient profile, Faxén's first law
gives $U=u_c (1-\tfrac23\lambda^2)=$
`{python} f"{faxen_velocity:.4f}"` at $\lambda=$
`{python} f"{particle_radius / R:.3f}"`. It is a free-space
result. At this blockage the walls matter, so we report it and do not gate on
it. The gated
reference is the series value $U_\text{free}=u_cK_P/K_H=$
`{python} f'{refs["force_free_velocity"]:.4f}'`.
The two-way passive velocity differs from it by
`{python} f"{passive_error:.2%}"`, against a
tolerance of `{python} f"{reference_tol:.2%}"`. That tolerance is the reference
uncertainty, floored
by twice the Oseen estimate of the inertial error. Two cautions apply. The two
series nearly
share their wall term, so their agreement with Faxén is not independent
evidence. And
$U_\text{free}=-F_0/F_1$ is a ratio of two forces that are both too low, so a
good passive velocity
does not show that the forces are right.
